title: You're back. That's what counts.
hook: You've been away a few days. No guilt trip here. Let's just pick up where you are.

screens.text: **Welcome back, {{convert.first_name}}.** Life got busy, or hard, or both. That happens to everyone, in week one or month three. No streaks to mourn, no lessons to catch up on. You're here now.

screens.prompt: What a few days away looks like
screens.text: Drag along the line. A dip isn't the end of the story. Coming back is the part that counts.

points.label: Going along
points.text: Praying, learning a little each day.

points.label: Life got in the way
points.text: Busy, hard, or both. A few days slipped by. It happens to everyone.

points.label: Today
points.text: You opened the app. That's the turn.

points.label: From here
points.text: The next prayer, one lesson a day, small and steady. The line keeps going up.

screens.title: Quick check-in
screens.intro: Four questions from lessons you've done. No pressure: it just shows what's fresh and what needs a look.

screens.text: **Allah is glad you're back.** The Prophet ﷺ said Allah is more pleased when His servant turns back to Him than a traveler who finds his lost camel, with all his food and water, in the middle of the desert [Muslim 2747].
bubbles: And when you take a step toward Allah, He comes toward you faster [Bukhari 7405].

screens.prompt: Coming back after a few days off, what's the first thing to do?

options.text: Pray the next prayer that's due, with what you know
options.feedback: Right. The next prayer is your fresh start. Everything else can follow.

options.text: Redo every lesson from the days you missed
options.feedback: Not quite. There's nothing to catch up on. Your next lesson is waiting, one a day as before.
Not quite. Feeling ready usually comes after you start, not before.

screens.title: Missed some prayers? Make them up (qada)
screens.intro: Missed prayers are made up: the same rak'ahs, as soon as you can [Bukhari 597].

steps.text: Pray each one you missed, with the same rak'ahs it has.
A few at a time is fine: add one with each prayer today.
Missed any on purpose? Say *astaghfirullah* ("I ask Allah's forgiveness") and move on.

screens.situation: Dre was away at a family event for three days and missed six prayers. He feels he has to pray all six tonight or he's "not a real Muslim."

options.text: Pray today's prayers on time, add one make-up with each, and finish the rest tomorrow
options.feedback: Yes. Steady and doable. Making them up a few at a time still counts fully.

options.text: Give up on the six; they're gone
options.feedback: Not quite. Missed prayers are made up [Bukhari 597], and a little at a time works.

options.text: Stay up past midnight praying all six, then sleep through Fajr
options.feedback: Not quite. Burning out tonight costs tomorrow. Small and steady beats a big push.

screens.text: **Small and steady wins.** The deeds Allah loves most are the ones done regularly, even if they're small [Bukhari 6464]. So don't try to make up for the gap with a huge burst.
bubbles: Five prayers, one lesson, one message to {{mentor.name}}. That's a full comeback.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Allah's joy at a servant's return [Muslim 2747]; He comes toward the one who comes toward Him [Bukhari 7405]; don't despair of His mercy [Q 39:53]; the best of those who err are those who repent [Tirmidhi 2499].
- The most beloved deeds are regular ones, even if small [Bukhari 6464].
- Missed prayers are made up when remembered [Bukhari 597]. Deliberately missing one is a sin, repaired by repentance plus the make-up; oversleeping or forgetting isn't a sin [First Instructions ch. 5]. Hanafi: with five or fewer owed, order is kept (missed before current) unless the current time is running out or they forgot; with six or more, order drops [SeekersGuidance (makeup order)]. No make-ups in the three disliked times (sunrise, zenith, sunset) in the Hanafi school (Day 21).
- Not made up: prayers from before Islam [IslamWeb 243298]; prayers missed during a period or postnatal bleeding.
- No lesson catch-up: the program resumes with the next lesson.

**Likely questions**
- *"I missed a lot."* Calm plan: today's five first, then one make-up with each prayer (or more if they can), in order where possible; for many weeks, escalate to the imam to count and plan. Never overwhelm.
- *"Is Allah angry with me?"* Lead with mercy: Muslim 2747, Q 39:53. Coming back is what He loves.
- *"How do I stop it happening again?"* One anchor: a fixed prayer (Fajr or Maghrib) as a daily non-negotiable, phone reminders, a friend or the mentor to check in with.
- *"I forgot how to pray."* Offer to walk through it or point to Day 3; the minimum prayer is enough to start.

**Escalate:** large numbers of missed prayers; anything suggesting depression, crisis or danger at home (safety rule first); a convert who says they want to leave Islam (calm, no pressure, offer the imam or a scholar).

**Don't**
- Don't mention streaks, missed days or how far "behind" they are.
- Don't ask why they were away; the reflection is optional.
- Don't use guilt or Hell to motivate.
madhabNote: - **Order of make-ups:** the Hanafi and Maliki schools require keeping order when only a few prayers are owed; the Shafi'i school recommends it; the Hanbali school requires it with some exceptions. Ask your imam if you have many to make up.
sourcesMd:
- [Muslim 2747](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2747): Allah's joy at His servant's repentance, more than a traveler finding his lost camel.
- [Bukhari 7405](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:7405): Allah comes nearer to the one who comes near to Him.
- [Bukhari 6464](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6464): the most beloved deeds are the most regular, even if small.
- [Bukhari 597](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:597): pray a forgotten prayer when you remember it.
- Qur'an [39:53](https://quran.com/39/53). [Tirmidhi 2499](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:2499) (hasan, al-Albani).
- First Instructions on Worship ch. 5 (missing the prayer time).
- [SeekersGuidance: the current prayer while make-ups are owed](https://seekersguidance.org/answers/hanafi-fiqh/what-is-the-ruling-of-a-current-prayer-while-leaving-the-make-up-prayers/).
- [IslamWeb 243298](https://www.islamweb.net/en/fatwa/243298/does-the-person-who-embraces-islam-have-to-perform-the-prayers-he-missed-on-that-day): no make-up for prayers before Islam.
